question: What is a tracheostomy?

options.A: A tube inserted through the nose into the stomach
options.B: A small incision made in the upper chest wall
options.C: A flexible scope passed down the throat
options.D: A surgical opening made into the trachea

explanation: A tracheostomy involves creating a surgical opening directly into the trachea through the neck. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: How does a tracheostomy differ from an endotracheal tube?

options.A: An endotracheal tube is always permanent
options.B: A tracheostomy bypasses the upper airway via the neck
options.C: A tracheostomy goes through the mouth and nose
options.D: An endotracheal tube requires no mechanical support

explanation: Endotracheal tubes enter through the mouth or nose, whereas tracheostomy tubes enter directly through a surgical neck incision. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h1)

question: What is a common reason a patient needs a tracheostomy?
explanation: Patients needing a ventilator for an extended period often receive a tracheostomy for safety and comfort. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h2)

question: Why would a patient with severe facial swelling get a tracheostomy instead of a normal breathing tube through the mouth?

options.A: It lets the patient speak normally right away
options.B: It bypasses the blocked upper airway completely
options.C: It stops all future lung infections completely
options.D: It needs zero nursing checks afterward

explanation: When facial trauma blocks the upper airway, a tracheostomy makes a fresh, clear pathway below the blockage. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is the job of the obturator in a tracheostomy kit?

options.A: To collect thick mucus from the lungs
options.B: To secure the ties around the patient's neck
options.C: To inflate and deflate the tracheal cuff
options.D: To guide smooth insertion of the tube without injury

explanation: Think of the obturator as a smooth guide! Its rounded tip helps slide the tracheostomy tube right into place without scratching the tissue. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why does a tracheostomy tube have a removable inner cannula?

options.A: It allows easy cleaning and removal of dried mucus
options.B: It acts as a backup if the patient stops breathing
options.C: It measures the exact pressure in the lungs
options.D: It allows the patient to talk without a valve

explanation: Mucus builds up fast! The inner cannula can be easily taken out and cleaned so the airway stays open and clear. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h3)

question: When is the right time to apply suction during tracheostomy suctioning?

options.A: While pushing the catheter down into the airway
options.C: Only while withdrawing and rotating the catheter
options.D: Before inserting any tubing into the stoma

explanation: Never apply suction on the way in! You only suction gently while twisting and pulling the catheter out to protect the delicate airway lining. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the most important safety rule when changing a patient's tracheostomy neck ties?

options.A: Have an assistant hold the tube in place
options.B: Do it quickly without washing hands
options.C: Inflate the cuff to maximum pressure

explanation: Always have a partner hold the tube securely during tie changes. One good cough can pop the tube right out! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h4)

question: What spare equipment must always stay right at the bedside for a patient with a tracheostomy?

options.A: A set of surgical scalpels and sutures
options.C: A spare tracheostomy tube and obturator
options.D: An extra oxygen tank and nasal cannula

explanation: Safety first! A matching spare tube and obturator must always be ready at the bedside in case of an emergency replacement. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h5)

question: A patient accidentally pulls out their fresh tracheostomy tube and panics. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Place a simple nasal cannula over the open stoma
options.B: Wait for the primary surgeon to arrive on the unit
options.C: Call for help and attempt to reinsert the tube or secure the airway

explanation: An accidental decannulation is an emergency! Call for help right away and try to reinsert the tube to keep the airway open. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h5)

question: In tracheostomy care, what does the term 'decannulation' mean?

options.A: Permanent removal of the tracheostomy tube
options.B: Inserting a new mechanical ventilation machine
options.C: Inflating the cuff to maximum pressure
options.D: Cleaning the inner cannula with sterile water

explanation: Decannulation simply means the tube is finally and permanently removed because the patient no longer needs it. You're mastering the terminology! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h6)

question: What generally happens to the tracheostomy hole (stoma) after the tube is permanently removed?

options.A: It requires major plastic surgery to sew shut
options.B: It naturally heals closed with a simple dressing
options.C: It must be plugged with a permanent metal cap
options.D: It remains permanently open for air passage

explanation: Nature is amazing! Covered with a simple dressing, the stoma usually shrinks and closes up on its own within a few days. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h6)
